description:
FILED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING; found by the #1737
probe table.

perl's INFIX `isa` operator (feature 'isa', 5.32+) requires a BLESSED
REFERENCE on the left.  Everything else is FALSE -- including a class NAME,
which the METHOD spelling accepts:

    use feature 'isa'; package Bar; sub new { bless {}, shift }
    package main; my $b = Bar->new;
    $b isa Bar      -> 1        Bar->isa("Bar")      -> 1
    "Bar" isa Bar   -> ''  <==  PCL answers 1
    [] isa Bar      -> ''       (PCL: '' since #1737)
    42 isa Zed      -> ''       (PCL: '' since #1737)
    undef isa Zed   -> ''       (PCL: '' since #1737)

So after #1737 nine of the ten probed shapes agree and this is the tenth.

WHERE: `Pl/ExprToCL.pm:1527` emits `(p-isa $left $right)` for the infix
operator -- the SAME runtime function the method spelling uses, and the two
have different rules about a non-ref invocant.  perl's pp_isa calls
`sv_derived_from_sv` only after `SvROK(left) && SvOBJECT(SvRV(left))`.

THE FIX SHAPE: not "another arm in p-isa" -- the discriminator is which
SPELLING was written, which only the emitter knows.  Either emit a distinct
`p-isa-infix` (one line, one new runtime function that checks blessedness then
calls p-isa), or pass a flag.  Read #1737's docstring first: p-isa is the
predicate BOTH the method arms and the infix operator call, and its contract
is "1 or '', never undef".

SIZE: no baseline row today (t/uni/universal.t does not use the infix
operator).  It is a silent wrong for code that writes `$maybe_class isa Foo`.
subject: the INFIX isa operator wants a BLESSED REFERENCE on the left -- "Bar" isa Bar is "" in perl and 1 in PCL, because the emitter routes it to the same p-isa the METHOD spelling uses
